items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: he told me he was going to get a little group together and he says, 'I want you to play the piano.' ... he put me on the piano

ctx.x: It's lucky I was reading the right things, you know, and so anyway, that was getting around my, you know, senior year, and so this fellow Mr. Collins -- you know, the one that had practically forced me to play there in school, he told me he was going to get a little group together and he says, "I want you to play the piano." And he got saxaphone, I think he had two trumpets and a couple of saxophones and a bass and a drum, you know, and he put me on the piano, you know, so I told him, I said, "I don't know…

So then he says, "The first thing I'm going to do, I'm going to have rehearsals out to your house." He knew who my people were, you know. So he had the rehearsal out to my house and so they thought, "Well, you know, maybe this ain't too bad. You know, Mr. Collins, he's teaching there and he teaches music." He brought these guys out here and he had a drummer, you know, but my folks enjoyed watching him drum and he'd be doing all this stuff and you know how --
